findings.title: Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive and unnormalized
findings.body: BlockedEmail.should_block? looks up the address with an exact equality match and never downcases or strips it. Mailbox providers treat the domain (and almost always the whole address) as case-insensitive, and signup stores whatever case the client sent (User.new_from_params assigns params[:email] raw, while change_email downcases). An attacker who is listed as blocked@evil.com can register Blocked@evil.com or " blocked@evil.com" and skip the block entirely. The unique index on blocked_emails.email has the same problem, so both casings can be stored as distinct rows.

findings.title: Domain whitelist/blacklist regex is unanchored and barely escaped
findings.body: email_in_restriction_setting? only escapes dots, then matches /@(#{domains})/i anywhere in the address with no end anchor. A whitelist of example.com therefore accepts user@example.com.attacker.com (and any other string that merely contains @example.com). The same pattern makes a blacklist miss or over-match, and any other regex metacharacter in the site setting (|, +, parentheses) is interpolated live, so a bad setting raises RegexpError and turns signup validation into a 500. This is the only enforcement of those settings after the check was moved off User.

findings.title: Block check writes match stats during validation
findings.body: should_block? increments match_count and saves the row as a side effect of validation. UsersController#create calls user.valid? and then user.save, and save validates again, so a matching do_nothing row is counted twice on every successful signup attempt. The increment is also a non-atomic read-modify-write, so concurrent signups lose updates. A failed or rolled-back user save still leaves the counter changed, because the BlockedEmail write is a separate commit. Stats and last_match_at cannot be trusted, and every email validation now does an extra write.

findings.title: Moved domain rules and real block lookup are untested
findings.body: EmailValidator is the new home of the whitelist/blacklist checks, but the spec only stubs BlockedEmail.should_block? and never exercises domain settings, case folding, or a real blocked row. The old User#email_validator tests were deleted with the method, so a whitelist bypass or a block that does not fire on User save would not be caught.
